title: What DSPM service registration covers: supported services, connection tests, Cosmos DB, on-premises file servers, NFS and LDAP

prose.text: {{supported-services}} The database, Snowflake and Databricks registration is in [[dspm.service-registration-databases]], and the scanning side is in [[dspm.scanning]] and [[dspm.overview]].

prose.label: Connection test status values.
prose.text: The test status values are not listed {{gap:test-status-values}}.

prose.label: Cosmos DB permissions.
prose.text: The exact data plane permissions are not listed {{gap:cosmos-permission-list}}.

prose.label: NFS client page.
prose.text: The ports table also carries rows the page does not explain {{gap:nfs-page-unexplained}}.

checks.do: Whether the connection test has been run manually for a Snowflake or Databricks service, which the page says DSPM does not run automatically.
Whether the file server type and protocol allow the field being filled: Authentication Type is available only for NetApp, and the LDAP server selection only for SMB.

supported-services.statement: DSPM service registration supports managed and unmanaged databases, Snowflake, on-premises file servers, Databricks workspaces and LDAP servers; unmanaged database servers can be added individually or in bulk with templates.

quotes: DSPM provides support for configuring managed and unmanaged databases, Snowflake, on-premises file servers, Databricks workspaces, and Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) servers.
You can add unmanaged database servers individually or in bulk using templates.

cosmos-nosql-api.statement: For Azure Cosmos DB, DSPM supports scanning resources through its NoSQL API.

quotes: Azure Cosmos DB: A globally distributed, multi-model database service from Microsoft. DSPM supports the scanning of resources using its NoSQL API.

auto-test-onprem.statement: DSPM runs the connection test automatically after registration for on-premises unmanaged databases; for Snowflake and Databricks the test must be run manually.

quotes: For on-premises unmanaged databases, DSPM runs the test automatically after registration.
For unmanaged databases, such as Snowflake and Databricks, you must run the test manually.

test-connection-scope.statement: The connection test checks network connectivity and credentials of a registered service before scans; the page says it is automatic for on-premises unmanaged databases and manual for cloud unmanaged databases, Snowflake and Databricks.

quotes: verify the network connectivity and credentials for registered services before performing data scans.
Testing the connection confirms that DSPM can access the service and credentials are valid, reducing scan failures.
For on-premises unmanaged databases, the connection is tested automatically after registration. For cloud unmanaged databases, Snowflake, and Databricks, manually initiate the connection test.

test-connection-results.statement: Test results appear on the service tab as Last Tested, Status and Status Message; the Status Message gives a description of the test result such as a connection timeout.

quotes: - Last Tested: The date and time the connection was last tested.
- Status: The test status.
- Status Message: A description of the test result (e.g., dial tcp ..*.*:: connect: connection timed out).

test-connection-tabs.statement: The connection test can be started from the Unmanaged Databases, Snowflake or Databricks tab, for one service or several selected services.

quotes: select the relevant tab (Unmanaged Databases, Snowflake, or Databricks).
To test the connection for multiple database services:

discovery-columns.statement: The On-Premises File Servers and LDAP Servers tabs show a Discovery Status of Completed, Failed or In Progress, with an Error column giving the reason discovery failed.

quotes: Discovery Status: The current status (Completed, Failed, In Progress) of the file server discovery process.
Error: The error message that indicates why the file servers could not be discovered.
Discovery Status: The current status (Completed, Failed, In Progress) of the server discovery process.
Error: The error message that indicates why the servers could not be discovered.

detected-shares.statement: On the On-Premises File Servers tab, Detected Shares is the number of file servers discovered during the last scan.

quotes: Detected Shares: The number of file servers discovered during the last scan.

cosmos-permissions-manual.statement: DSPM does not configure Azure Cosmos DB data plane permissions automatically; they are granted manually, using the Terraform template or Azure CLI command from the Admin Console.

quotes: To perform data plane scanning, you must manually grant the necessary read permissions in your Azure environment to DSPM. DSPM does not configure data plane permissions automatically.
You can use the Terraform template or an Azure CLI command available in the Zscaler Admin Console and apply it to the Cosmos DB accounts.

cosmos-prereq.statement: Registering Cosmos DB accounts requires the Microsoft Entra tenant hosting them to be onboarded to DSPM.

quotes: The Microsoft Entra tenant hosting the Cosmos DB accounts is onboarded to DSPM.

cosmos-terraform-vs-cli.statement: The Terraform template applies permissions across multiple Cosmos DB accounts and creates a custom data plane reader role assigned to the scanner managed identity; the Azure CLI command configures a single account.

quotes: Use a Terraform template for the DSPM integration and to apply permissions across multiple accounts at the same time.
This script creates the necessary custom data plane reader role and assigns it to the DSPM scanner's managed identity role.
Use a CLI command to configure permissions for an individual Azure Cosmos DB account.

cosmos-failure-and-removal.statement: If Cosmos DB permissions are not granted, scans fail with a permissions error in the scan logs; removing access means deleting the role assignment in Azure, with no action in the Admin Console.

quotes: If permissions are not granted using one of the preceding methods, the scans fail and an error message is displayed in the scan logs indicating a permissions issue.
To remove DSPM's access to a registered Azure Cosmos DB account, you must manually delete the role assignment within your Azure environment.
No action is required in the Zscaler Admin Console to remove an Azure Cosmos DB account registration.

databricks-edit-effective-next-scan.statement: Changes to the Databricks configuration take effect at the next scheduled scan.

quotes: Any changes to the Databricks configuration take effect at the next scheduled scan.

delete-confirm.statement: Deleting a Databricks workspace or account in the Admin Console requires typing CONFIRM in the confirmation window.

quotes: read the message, and then enter CONFIRM in the text box.

prereqs.statement: Before adding an on-premises file server, an on-premises scanner must be integrated, a data center created and associated with the scanner, the NFS client configured for NFS-based servers, and an LDAP server added to map identities to file share entitlements; the file server's own LDAP server selection is optional and available only for SMB.

quotes: Integrate an on-premises scanner with DSPM to enable scanning of on-premises file servers.
Create an on-premises data center and associate it with the configured on-premises scanner.
Configure the Network File System (NFS) client on the scanner host before you add NFS-based file servers.
Add a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) server for DSPM to map identities to file share entitlements.
4. LDAP Server (available only when SMB is selected as the protocol):
- Server (Optional): Select the registered LDAP server for the on-premises file server.

types-and-defaults.statement: File server type choices are Windows, Linux or NetApp for NFS and Windows or NetApp for SMB; the default ports are 445 for SMB and 2049 for NFS, and a custom port can be entered.

quotes: - NFS: Select Windows, Linux, or NetApp.
- SMB: Select Windows, or NetApp.
- Default Port: SMB uses 445 and NFS uses 2049.
- Custom Port: Enter a valid port number based on your configuration requirements.

version-and-hostname.statement: The NFS version field appears only when the NFS protocol is selected; for NFS with the NetApp file server type, only a hostname is entered.

quotes: Version (available only if NFS protocol is selected): Select the NFS version to use.
- For an NFS protocol and NetApp file server type, enter the hostname only.

auth-availability.statement: Authentication Type (Kerberos, AUTH_SYS, NTLMv2) is available only for NetApp file servers: Kerberos for NFS or SMB, AUTH_SYS for NFS only, NTLMv2 for SMB only.

quotes: | Authentication Type | Available only when NetApp is selected as the file server type. |
| Kerberos | Available for NFS or SMB protocol with NetApp file server type. |
| AUTH_SYS | Available for NFS protocol with NetApp file server type only. |
| NTLMv2 | Available for SMB protocol with NetApp file server type only. |

creds-and-gids.statement: Username applies to Windows or Linux file servers, or to NetApp with Kerberos or NTLMv2; Group IDs (comma-separated GIDs) apply only with AUTH_SYS.

quotes: | Username | Available for Windows or Linux file server types, or when Kerberos or NTLMv2 is selected for NetApp. |
| Group IDs | Available only when AUTH_SYS is selected as the Authentication Type. |
Group IDs: Enter one or more GIDs that have access to the file share, separated by commas.

ldap-selection-smb.statement: The optional LDAP server selection on a file server is available only for the SMB protocol.

quotes: 4. LDAP Server (available only when SMB is selected as the protocol):
- Server (Optional): Select the registered LDAP server for the on-premises file server.

post-add-discovery.statement: After a file server is added DSPM starts discovering it, and a discovery failure is shown in the Error column.

quotes: DSPM starts to discover the file servers. If the discovery process fails, an error message is displayed in the Error column.

edit-timing.statement: Changes to an on-premises file server take effect only at the next scheduled scan.

quotes: Changes made to the on-premises file server configuration take effect only at the next scheduled scan.

nfs-support-kerberos.statement: DSPM supports NFS shares hosted on Linux and Windows servers, using Kerberos for authentication, which requires configuring the Key Distribution Center (KDC).

quotes: DSPM supports Network File System (NFS) shares hosted on Linux and Windows servers to discover and classify sensitive data. NFS uses Kerberos for authentication, and you must configure the Key Distribution Center (KDC) that allows the DSPM scanner to scan files for sensitive data.

nfs-ports.statement: NFS client configuration lists ports 53 TCP/UDP (DNS), 88 TCP/UDP (Kerberos), 111 and 2049 TCP/UDP (NFS portmapper and mount) and 135 TCP (RPC) from the VNet in its ports table.

quotes: | 53 | TCP/UDP | VNet | AD domain controller | DNS |
| 88 | TCP/UDP | VNet | AD domain controller | Kerberos |
| 111, 2049 | TCP/UDP | VNet | NFS SERVER | NFS Portmapper & Mount |
| 135 | TCP | VNet | AD domain controller | RPC |

nfs-linux-kdc.statement: On a Linux KDC, a Kerberos principal nfs/<scanner hostname> is created with addprinc -randkey, plus a read-only principal whose credentials are given when registering the file server.

quotes: - Linux KDC Server Using Kerberos
kadmin.local: addprinc -randkey nfs/zscaler_scanner_hostname
- Note the read-only username and password, and provide these details while registering the file server.

nfs-windows-kdc.statement: On Windows AD, a read-only user is created with uidNumber and gidNumber 1000 and a scanner computer account with uidNumber and gidNumber 0.

quotes: 2. uidNumber: 1000
3. gidNumber: 1000
2. uidNumber: 0
3. gidNumber: 0

ldap-purpose.statement: An LDAP server lets DSPM discover identities (users, groups, computer accounts) and entitlement data needed to analyze permissions on file shares.

quotes: enables DSPM to scan and discover identities (users, groups, and computer accounts) that have permissions to access sensitive data.
Adding an LDAP server allows DSPM to discover identity and entitlement data stored in the LDAP server
which is required for scanning and analyzing permissions on file shares to map user access and identify potential security risks accurately.

ldap-type-cert.statement: The LDAP server type selectable is Active Directory, and a PEM Root CA certificate can optionally be uploaded to verify the server SSL certificate.

quotes: 2. Server Type: Select Active Directory.
If your LDAP server uses a certificate, upload the PEM file to verify the LDAP server's SSL certificate for secure connection.

ldap-smb-entitlements.statement: A registered LDAP server can be selected when adding an on-premises file server, to analyze entitlements assigned to identities in SMB file shares.

quotes: You can select this server when adding an on-premises file server to analyze entitlements assigned to identities in SMB file shares.

test-status-values.title: Which Status values the connection test reports
test-status-values.detail: The Test Connection page names the Last Tested, Status and Status Message columns but does not enumerate the Status values.

cosmos-permission-list.title: Which data plane permissions the Cosmos DB role holds
cosmos-permission-list.detail: The page says the Terraform template or CLI command grants the necessary read permissions but does not list them.

nfs-page-unexplained.title: What the extra NFS client port rows and NSG default rules mean
nfs-page-unexplained.detail: The ports table includes SSH 22 and RDP 3389 rows for admin access, a default-rules Network Security Group is mentioned without a definition, and setspn -L is given without expected output.
